title: Tilt Illusion by Phase
description: EEG recordings from 36 participants performing an orientation discrimination task in a visual tilt illusion paradigm. A central target grating, titrated to appear vertical on average, was surrounded by an annular grating tilted by ±30 degrees. The dataset supports analysis of prestimulus EEG correlates, including alpha oscillation power and phase, of increased or decreased tilt illusion strength.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a Biosemi Active 2 system using 64 scalp electrodes and 6 EOG electrodes. Participants judged the tilt of a briefly presented (8.3 ms, 60% contrast) central grating by pressing left or right arrow keys. The angle of the central grating was first titrated to each participant's perceived vertical, separately for each surround. A mask of combined gratings was shown between trials to prevent buildup of tilt aftereffects. Original BDF files were converted to EEGLAB .set/.fdt format for BIDS.
